title: Configuration trace of a two-pass scan
statement: Let $k\in\mathbb N$, let $\Gamma$ be a symbol type, let $A$ be a state type, let $x,w$ be finite words over $\Gamma$, choose a work-tape index $i<k$, two transducers $\delta_f,\delta_b:A\times\Gamma\to A\times\Gamma$, an initial state $a_0$, and a configuration $d$ of the scan machine on input $x$. Suppose $d$ is in forward state $a_0$ and, on tape $i$, every cell at offset $p$ from its head contains the corresponding symbol of $w$ for $-1\le p\le |w|$, with cells outside the word blank. After $2|w|+2$ steps, the machine is in the done state carrying the final state of the two-pass transducer scan, and tape $i$ contains that scan's output in the $|w|$ cells starting at its original head position; every other tape cell retains its original content. At every earlier time $t<2|w|+2$ the state is not done, and throughout these steps tape $i$'s head stays between one cell left of its initial position and the cell $|w|$ to its right, while all other tape heads remain fixed.
hypotheses_covered: initial state of $d$ is the forward state carrying $a_0$
tape $i$ initially agrees with the buffered word at every offset from $-1$ through $|w|$
